newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares fall sharply on diplomatic row.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares fall sharply on diplomatic row.

text.p: Singapore shares fell 21 points, losing more than one percent in early Thursday trade, as the market reacted to a diplomatic row between the island republic and Malaysia, dealers said.
"The market is taking its cue from the row with Malaysia over SM Lee's comments," a dealer with a Singapore firm said.

On Wednesday Malaysian newspapers reported Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's description of Malaysia's Johor state as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in an affidavit filed in a Singapore court on January 27 in relation to libel action against an opposition politician.
Malaysia has asked for a retraction and apology.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index reacted badly to the row and stood at 2,155.91, down 21.48 at 0250 GMT.
The diplomatic row eclipsed poor industrial output figures released on Wednesday that showed total manufacturing output fell 7.2 percent year on year in January.
"The headlines over Malaysia coupled with the bad figures -- well its not good news," another dealer said.
Poor electronics output figures, down 10.9 percent year on year, pushed Creative Technology down Singapore $0.60 to S$14.90.
